security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, generated JSON text, and hardcoded subprocess calls with shell disabled. The script performs expected local resource detection and writes a local report. Semantic review found an embedded self-audit safety claim and promotional steering to an external service.

remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_output.json from published skill packages. Marketplace audits should rely on source behavior, not bundled safety claims.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted service
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web promotion from runtime skill instructions, or move it to transparent marketplace metadata.

remediation.issue: Custom output path can overwrite files
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting existing files and prefer the default project-local .claude_resources.json output path.

content.value_statement: Scientific workloads can fail when hardware limits are unknown. This skill detects local resources and recommends practical compute strategies before work starts.
actual_capabilities: Detects physical and logical CPU cores, architecture, processor name, and frequency when available.
Reports total, available, and used memory, including swap space details.
Checks disk capacity and free space for the current working directory.
Detects NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPU availability through local system utilities.
Writes a local resource report and generates compute strategy recommendations.
limitations: GPU detection depends on system utilities such as nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, or system_profiler.
Memory and disk results are snapshots and can change during a workflow.
The skill reports local resources only and does not monitor remote clusters.
Recommendations use fixed thresholds and may need adjustment for specialized workloads.

use_cases.title: Plan Large Dataset Processing
use_cases.description: Check memory and disk space before choosing pandas, Dask, Zarr, or streaming methods.

use_cases.title: Select Model Training Hardware
use_cases.description: Detect CUDA, ROCm, Metal, or CPU-only environments before configuring training libraries.

use_cases.title: Set Parallel Worker Counts
use_cases.description: Use CPU core counts to choose practical worker limits for scientific batch jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Resource Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run get-available-resources before this analysis. Tell me available CPU cores, memory, disk space, and whether GPU acceleration is available.

prompt_templates.title: Memory Strategy Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get-available-resources, then choose pandas, Dask, Zarr, or streaming for a dataset that may exceed memory.

prompt_templates.title: Training Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Run get-available-resources and recommend a training configuration for my model, including device choice and worker count.

prompt_templates.title: Workflow Execution Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get-available-resources to build an execution plan for a large scientific workflow with parallel steps, intermediate files, and fallback strategies.

output_examples.input: Check this workstation before I process a large imaging dataset.
output: The system has enough CPU cores for moderate parallel processing.
Available memory is limited for full in-memory loading, so chunked processing is recommended.
Disk space is sufficient for intermediate files, but cleanup should be planned.

output_examples.input: Tell me whether I can use GPU acceleration for this model run.
output: A local GPU backend is available and can be used for supported training libraries.
The response recommends the matching device family and keeps a CPU fallback option.

output_examples.input: Plan worker counts for a parameter sweep.
output: The response uses detected logical cores to recommend a worker count below full saturation.
It also warns when limited memory should reduce the number of concurrent tasks.

best_practices: Run detection before major compute tasks, not after failures appear.
Re-run detection when system load, machine type, or available storage changes.
Treat recommendations as starting points and adjust them for workload behavior.
anti_patterns: Assuming one resource report stays accurate throughout a long workflow.
Using maximum CPU workers when memory is the true bottleneck.
Ignoring missing GPU utility warnings and assuming acceleration is available.

faq.question: What does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects local CPU, memory, disk, operating system, Python version, and supported GPU indicators.

faq.question: Does it send resource data to a server?
faq.answer: No evidence found of network transmission. The script writes a local resource report.

faq.question: What dependency is required?
faq.answer: The Python script requires psutil. GPU checks also depend on vendor utilities being installed.

faq.question: Can I choose the output file?
faq.answer: Yes. The script supports a custom output path, but the default report stays in the current directory.

faq.question: Will results stay current?
faq.answer: No. Memory, disk, and GPU availability can change, so rerun detection before important tasks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
